parameter_definitions: 'existing' - capacity that was assumed to exist in the beginning of the solve. 'invested' - Capacity that comes online in the period. 'in_construction' - Capacity decided but not yet operating in the period. 'retired' - capacity the model decided to retire in the beginning of the given period. 'total' - sum of existing, invested and retired capacities.

per-entity annualized cost broken down by category (commodity cost, commodity sales, co2, other operational, starts, ramps, investment / retirement, fixed cost pre-existing / invested / reduction of divestments and, for nodes, upward / downward slack penalty). Fuel / commodity cost is attributed to the consuming process and CO2 cost is summed over every priced group the process touches. Summing a category over all entities reproduces the system-wide cost_annualized.
per-entity net present (discounted) cost over the horizon, same category break-down as cost_annualized. Summing a category over all entities reproduces the system-wide cost_discounted_total.

Marginal cost to invest in one more kW of capacity (zero value means that the model has invested in optimal amount; negative value means that if the model would be able to invest more, it could reduce total cost by the stated amount per kW; positive value means the cost is higher than the benefit by the stated amount per kW).
average online status of the connection (average number of units of the connection online during the period); only for connections with a startup_method.
online status of the connection (number of units of the connection online in each timestep); only for connections with a startup_method.
cumulative number of connection startups during the period; only for connections with a startup_method.

[per unit] average capacity factor of the flow, i.e. the utilization rate of the connection where flows in both directions are considered as utilization. Average of the absolute flow [MWh/h] divided by the capacity of the connection.
annualized cumulative flow through the connection (left to right is positive).
flow through the connection (left to right is positive).
annualized cumulative flow through the connection only to the left (first) node.
flow through the connection to the left (first) node.
annualized cumulative flow through the connection only to the right (second) node.
flow through the connection to the right (second) node.
how many tonnes of CO2 annualized the units and connections in this group have generated (by using commodity with CO2 content) or removed.
Share of VRE generation in the group of nodes (sum of 'upper_limit' flows into nodes divided by the sum of inflexible inflow (parameter 'inflow') into those nodes).
produces grouped and annualized flow results of the `node` members of the `group`
produces grouped flow results to the `node` members of the `group`

A set of period results for all node members of the group. Each share is a ratio of two energies summed over the period's time steps, weighted by the time-step weights (not an average of the time-step shares). '1. Loss of load share' - [0-1] upward slack / inflow. '2. VRE share of demand' - [>= 0] generation of the VRE units (units using an 'upper_limit' profile) into the member nodes / inflow. '3. Excess load share' - [0-1] downward slack / inflow. '4. Curtailed VRE of demand' - [>= 0] curtailed VRE / inflow. '5. Annualized inflow' - [MWh] inflow to the member nodes scaled to a year. '6. Curtailed VRE of potential VRE' - [0-1] curtailed VRE / potential VRE generation of the profiled VRE units into the member nodes.
Largest individual flow coming into a group of nodes that are part of the same inertia group.
the amount of inertia (MWs) in the group of nodes in each timestep.
the amount of inertia in the flows between the units and the nodes in the group.
use of slack variable and the associated penalty cost to meet the capacity margin requirement in the period.

The capacity margin of each solve with investment periods, per investment period at the group's binding step (the step with the largest deficit; which step it is, is in the capacity_margin__d CSV / parquet table, not here). 'margin' - [MW] the margin above demand. 'peak_demand' - [MW] the peak demand of the period. 'demand' - [MW] the demand at the binding step. 'requirement' - [MW] margin + demand. 'firm', 'vre' - [MW] the counted capacity of firm and VRE units. 'storage_flow', 'unit_flow', 'connections_net', 'consumption' - [MW] the flows of storage-backed units (minus the slack energy of their storage nodes), other units counted by their flow, connections and consumption. 'dumped' - [MW] minus the downward slack. 'counted' - [MW] the sum of the counted terms. 'shortfall' - [MW] the capacity the group lacked: max(0, requirement - counted). 'penalty_cost' - [M CUR] the penalty of the shortfall. 'capacity_price' - [CUR/kW/a] the shadow price of the margin.

[MW] What each unit, connection and node counts in the capacity margin of the group at its binding step, keyed 'class__entity' (class firm, vre, storage, storage_slack, unit_by_flow, connection, consumption or dumped); the values sum to the counted capacity. The binding step is in the capacity_margin_entity__d CSV / parquet table.
use of slack variable and the associated penalty cost to fulfill the inertia requirement in each timestep.
use of slack variable and the associated penalty cost to fulfill the non-synchronous share maximum share constraint in each timestep.
Annualized sum of flows in the group (members from group__connection__node and group__unit__node). Annualization scales the sum to correspond with full year time series.
Sum of flows in the group (members from group__connection__node and group__unit__node).
use of slack variable and the associated penalty cost to fulfill the upward or downward reserve requirement in each timestep.

[MW] The reserve requirement of the group in each timestep, from its requirement rows evaluated at the solution, keyed by quantity. 'requirement' - the need of the binding requirement row (the row with the largest need - counted; without a shortfall it can be below another method's need, the largest need is the largest requirement_<method>). 'requirement_timeseries', 'requirement_dynamic', 'requirement_n_1' - the need of each method the group has (n-1: the largest failure). 'provided' - the reserve of the group's providers (reserve x unitsize x reliability). 'counted' - the reserve the binding row counts (for an n-1 row, without the failing process's own reserve), so shortfall = requirement - counted when there is a shortfall. 'shortfall' - the requirement not met. The per-provider breakdown is in the reserve__group__provider__dt CSV / Excel table, not here.

[MW] The reserve requirement of the group in each period, keyed by quantity: 'requirement_avg', 'provided_avg', 'counted_avg', 'shortfall_avg' - the time-step-weighted averages over the period's realized steps where the reserve was modelled (compare requirement_avg with counted_avg: with an n-1 requirement the failing process's own reserve is in provided, not in counted); 'requirement_max', 'shortfall_max' - the largest step values.

Annualized (scaled to one year) and undiscounted cost for each period. The costs are divided into the following categories: 'unit investment/retirement' - [CUR] cost of investing in unit capacity or benefits from salvaging unit capacity. 'connection investment/retirement' - [CUR] cost of investing in connection capacity or benefits from salvaging connection capacity. 'storage investment/retirement' - [CUR] cost of investing in storage capacity or benefits from salvaging storage capacity. 'commodity' - [CUR] cost of unit using commodity inputs or benefit of selling commodities (negative value). 'CO2' - [CUR] cost of CO2 emissions caused by unit using commodities with CO2 content. 'variable cost' - [CUR] other variable operation and maintenance costs. 'starts' - [CUR] start up costs. 'ramps' - [CUR] ramp costs, the cost of changing the flow of units with a ramp_cost. 'upward penalty' - [CUR] cost of involuntary demand reduction. 'downward penalty' - [CUR] cost of involuntary demand increase- 'inertia penalty' - [CUR] cost of not meeting the inertia constraint. 'non-synchronous penalty' - [CUR] cost of not meeting the non-synchronous constraint. 'capacity margin penalty' - [CUR] cost of not meeting the capacity margin constraint. 'upward reserve penalty' - [CUR] cost of not meeting the upward reserve constraint. 'downward reserve penalty' - [CUR] cost of not meeting the downward reserve constraint.

Includes seven parameters that form the ramp room envelope (how much there is additional room to ramp in a give node). 'ramp' - [MW] the actual ramp in the node from previous timestep to this timestep.
'units_up' - [MW] additional room for upward ramps from non-VRE units connected to the node. 'VRE_up' - [MW] adds upward ramp room from VRE units on top of the ramp room from non-VRE units. 'connections_up' - [MW] adds upward ramp room from connections on top of the previous ramp rooms (does not consider whether the connected node has ramp room, but is simply the available capacity in the connection). 'units_down' - [MW] additional room for downward ramps from non-VRE units connected to the node. 'VRE_down' - [MW] adds downward ramp room from VRE units on top of the ramp room from non-VRE units. 'connections_down' - [MW] adds downward ramp room from connections on top of the previous ramp rooms (does not consider whether the connected node has ramp room, but is simply the available capacity in the connection).
storage state of the node in each timestep.
